author: kevaundray
content:
Doesn't having multiple bindings in seacast mean we will have deadcode in libraries?

ie I imagine that once we do seacast with waggle, seacast with libp2p would not make sense?

author: cskiraly
content: That depends on how it is phrased in the spec. If you make all bindings a must, that yes. I don't intend to do that. The goal is not "live cross-compatibility", but spec quality.

author: cskiraly
content: networking is full of potocols that could run above and bewlow various thigs. Deesn't mean your laptop goes on sub-ghz wireless, for example

author: kevaundray
content: why do the specs need to state something that noone will use?

author: kevaundray
content: Maybe I'm misunderstanding your point

author: cskiraly
content: I think you do

author: cskiraly
content: The bindings are examples

author: cskiraly
content: We can lift one or the other to mandatory in a given embodiment

author: cskiraly
content: This is how it was done for decades, for a reason

author: kevaundray
content: But is it clear that in production, clients will only ever need seacast with one of (Gossipsub, Waggle, libp2p streams, QUIC) ?

author: cskiraly
content: Are you writing monolithic program, or believe in some moldularity? Kind of the same point, although a different variety

author: cskiraly
content: actually wouldn't bet on that. Let me find an image for you ...

author: cskiraly
content: It is not exactly the same point, but there are practicalities around how network protocl versions and forks interact that are not trivial

author: cskiraly
content: We do have TPC and QUIC in parallel today. While one might say that's not ideal, these things happen as compromises

author: kevaundray
content:
I think modularity is good, my question was on why the specs need to spec interactions between components we won’t use?

Unless we plan to do seacast with libp2p and also seacast with quic etc, but this doesn’t seem like it’s the plan. ie aren’t we just going to do seacast with waggle?

author: kevaundray
content: I wouldn’t say this is the same thing, because quic is being introduced and we need to support both for a while

author: cskiraly
content: ok, we go in circles a bit. The bindings are a demonstration of the maturity of the abstractions. It is a tool. It is common practice. It does not say anything about how we will use it

author: vladimir_ea
content: So, if I understand, the idea of multiple bindings is to be able to evaluate different approaches? Then we should agree which to adopt?

author: taulepton_
content: how do the bindings for gossipsub work? Isn't there an overlap in terms of topology dissemination logic between gossipsub and seacast?

author: kevaundray
content: This would make sense to me, then after experimentation I would remove the other protocols that we don’t use so we don’t maintain them

author: cskiraly
content: So each binding has a sort of an "exception list" on features. Each comes with its compromises and powers. Not that many, but there are obvious diffs

author: taulepton_
content: In my mind I kind of see it as QUIC = transport, waggle = API, seacast = dissemination logic. Am I thinking about this correctly?

author: taulepton_
content:
to group comprehensively:
transport: QUIC
API: (libp2p, waggle)
logic: (gossipsub, seacast)

I know this is a massive simplification and you can frankenstein these layers in different ways but broadly speaking this is my conceptual model
